clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old male presented with a five-month history of left second toe pain, numbness, tingling, burning sensation, continued pain, dry gangrene, and non-healing wounds, initially misdiagnosed as mild PAD. Initial workup at a vascular clinic included PVRs, ABI, TBI, CTA of the abdomen with runoff, and MRI of the left foot. CTA (E004) revealed a vascular malformation measuring 3.4 cm x 2.7 cm x 10.8 cm overlying the midshaft of the fibula and within the left fibularis brevis and longus muscles, while showing normal abdominal aorta and patent iliac, femoral, and popliteal arteries. Duplex ultrasound (E005) further characterized this as having low-resistance arterial flow within the malformation, and PVRs/ABI/TBI (E002) showed normal ABIs but mild distal PAD based on TBI. Diagnostic angiography (E006) definitively confirmed a large, complex left lower-extremity arteriovenous malformation (AVM) with feeding vessels from the anterior tibial, peroneal, and posterior tibial arteries. The patient subsequently underwent transarterial embolization with ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer and embolization coils (E006), with a final angiogram (E007) showing significantly reduced flow to the AVM.

Duplex ultrasound revealed low-resistance arterial flow within the vascular malformation, consistent with an AVM.
Diagnostic angiography confirmed a large, complex left lower-extremity AVM with feeding vessels from the anterior tibial, peroneal, and posterior tibial arteries.
The patient underwent transarterial embolization with ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer and embolization coils.
